LESSON: READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we read narratives?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension
2. apply appropriate reading strategies to read a narrative of about 320 words for information
3. appreciate reading for purposes of comprehension and information

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply appropriate reading strategies to read a narrative of about 320 words for information

What this means
In this part you learn to apply appropriate reading strategies to read a narrative of about 320 words for information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply appropriate reading strategies to read a narrative of about 320 words for information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply appropriate reading strategies to read a narrative of about 320 words for information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate reading for purposes of comprehension and information

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate reading for purposes of comprehension and information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate reading for purposes of comprehension and information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate reading for purposes of comprehension and information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading to a partner. (skill: apply appropriate reading strategies to read a narrative of about 320 words for information)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate reading for purposes of comprehension and information)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: apply appropriate reading strategies to read a narrative of about 320 words for information.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate reading for purposes of comprehension and information.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we read narratives?
2. What makes you enjoy reading a narrative?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension.
5. Be able to: apply appropriate reading strategies to read a narrative of about 320 words for information.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
